status: Coherent shared Celery/logging diagnostic tranche verified and source-frozen; whole dashboard audit remains open
manual_scope: All8changed/current runtime owners fully physically reviewed. Installed SDK files were read only in enumerated trace/task/backend/loader/Request/strategy/consumer sections; not counted as full SDK-file reviews.
source_to_sink: A real synthetic SQLite trigger -> SQLAlchemy IntegrityError (hide_parameters=True hides bound params but not DB-origin detail) -> real task trace -> automatic log context/data + exception traceback -> upstream result serialization/store. New projections run before formatting and before store_result encoding, not post-save signals.

Task body/kwargs -> publication repr headers, retry signature options, legacy Request/context fallback -> received/earlyfailure/retry/success event/log representations. Actual args/kwargs remain unchanged at every execution/publication assertion.
Invalid message -> Consumer.on_unknown_message before any Request exists -> raw body log. Actual expected-red test qualified the extra pre-format guard; reject behavior remains intact.
preserved_behavior: Actual exception objects/args, Retry/Reject/Ignore/admission decisions, requeue/countdown/retry count and actual payloads remain intact. Celery's existing conversion of a keyword-only admission exception into its pickleable RuntimeError parent is matched, not mistaken for a new app defect.

Task/result statuses, success business results, result schema type/module identity, upstream successful-result deduplication and Redis persistence paths remain delegated to Celery. Framework status/failure handling is not disabled.

App identity, broker/backend URLs, Redis/TLS connection parameters, queues, routes, serializers, schedules, worker bounds and task declarations remain unchanged; factory reconstruction is explicitly tested.
Known safe provider error codes and value-free source module/function/line frames remain useful. Diagnostic projections omit private values, original source lines/paths and raw exception strings.

verification.coverage: Fresh isolated branch coverage,57affected cases.8module line coverage92.59–100%; minimum90proposed for all8, no previous budget floor modified.
verification.failed_intermediate_evidence: Initial admission fixture assertion incorrectly expected Celery to retain a non-pickleable keyword-only exception instance; corrected against upstream Retry baseline. Two one/four-case cov-append invocations hit warning-as-error for an explicitly named unimported loader. No warning filters added; final coherent57-case directory-target coverage passes without those instrumentation errors.

limits: No live broker, Redis server, provider, PostgreSQL driver or real private payloads exercised. Actual SQLite errors, upstream eager/worker-like tracing, in-memory CacheBackend persistence, received strategy and Request events are exercised.

EagerResult and signal/task in-process exceptions retain original objects/details by design; changing those would alter business classification. The fixed sinks are configured automatic logs/events and persisted failure diagnostics.

Default result_extended=False does not persist task args/kwargs in backend metadata; this was not claimed as an observed backend kwargs leak. Explicitly enabling extended result metadata remains a separate privacy-sensitive configuration boundary; actual broker payloads and successful business results necessarily remain private application data.
Historical logs/result entries are not erased or rewritten. Existing result expiry/retention behavior is unchanged.
This does not claim every arbitrary application logger or future third-party Celery signal consumer is private; changes cover the demonstrated configured automatic task diagnostic sinks.
